transcript.text:
A freezer that keeps beeping is usually warning about one of these:

1. Door not fully closed
• Check for food packages, ice buildup, or a drawer preventing closure.
• Wipe the door gasket/seal and make sure it contacts all the way around.
• Press the door inward firmly for 10–20 seconds to see if the alarm stops.

2. Temperature too high
• The target freezer temperature is usually 0°F / -18°C.
• This can happen after a power cut, leaving the door open, adding lots of warm groceries, or a failing cooling system.
• Keep the door shut as much as possible and allow several hours to recover.

3. Door switch problem
• Find the small switch around the door frame that detects when the door is closed. Press and release it a few times; it may be stuck or iced over.
• If the interior light stays on with the door shut, the switch may be faulty.

4. Power or control-panel alert
• Unplug the freezer (or switch it off at the breaker) for about 5 minutes, then restart it—only if food is still cold/frozen and you can do so safely.
• Some models have an Alarm, Reset, or Mute button. Muting the beep does not fix the underlying temperature issue.

5. Fault code / mechanical issue
• Look at the display for a code such as “E,” “Er,” “HI,” or a flashing temperature.
• Check that vents inside the freezer are not blocked and that the exterior condenser area is not packed with dust.

Food safety: If items are still hard-frozen or have ice crystals, they are generally okay. If the freezer has been above 40°F / 4°C for over 2 hours, discard perishable foods.

If you tell me the brand/model, what the display says, and whether it beeps continuously or at intervals, I can narrow it down.
It's a Bosch. The freezer temperature number is flashing and there's a red alarm symbol. Beeps non-stop, started this morning.

On Bosch freezers, a flashing temperature with a red alarm symbol and continuous beeping normally means the freezer temperature has risen above the safe alarm threshold. The alarm can usually be silenced, but it will remain indicated until the temperature comes back down.

Try this:

1. Silence the alarm
• Press the Alarm button, or on some Bosch models press/hold the red alarm symbol or the temperature button for a few seconds.
• This only stops the noise—it does not clear the warning until the freezer is cold again.

2. Check the door and seal
• Make sure no food, drawer, ice, or packaging is holding the door open.
• Inspect the rubber gasket all around; clean any debris and make sure it seals evenly.
• Check that drawers are pushed fully in.

3. Check the displayed temperature
• Normal target is about 0°F / -18°C.
• If the display is flashing a much warmer temperature, leave the door closed and give it time to recover.
• If you loaded groceries, had the door open for a long time, or had a brief power interruption, it may take several hours—sometimes up to 24 hours to return to normal.

4. Use Super Freeze, if available
• Turn on Super Freeze / SuperFrost. It temporarily runs the compressor harder and can help it recover. Turn it off once the freezer is back at temperature.

5. Check whether it is actually cooling
• Listen for the compressor/fan running.
• Make sure internal air vents are not covered by food.
• If it is warm inside, not making cooling sounds, or the temperature is continuing to climb, keep the door shut and arrange service.

Food: if food is still solidly frozen or still has ice crystals, it is generally safe to keep/refreeze. If items have completely thawed and have been warmer than 40°F / 4°C for more than about 2 hours, discard perishable items.

If the alarm started without a power cut, door being left open, or warm food being added—and especially if it has not begun dropping after a few hours—possible causes include a failed fan, iced-up evaporator, compressor/start issue, or temperature sensor fault. The model number from the label inside the freezer would let you identify the exact alarm-control method.

Pressed the bell button and the beeping stopped. The bottom drawer wasn't pushed in properly last night, a bag was sticking out. I've shut it now. Display says -9 and is going down slowly. Seal looks fine.

That fits a door-left-ajar temperature alarm. At -9°C, the freezer is still warmer than its normal -18°C setting, but if the number is gradually dropping after you shut the drawer/door, it is recovering normally.

What to do now:

• Keep the door closed as much as possible for the next several hours.
• Turn on Super Freeze if your Bosch has it; it can speed recovery.
• Avoid adding warm food until it is back near -18°C.
• Check again in 2–4 hours. It should continue moving downward. Full recovery can take overnight, especially if it was open for much of the night.
• The red alarm/light should clear once the freezer reaches a safe temperature; on some models you may need to press the alarm button again after it is cold.

Food should generally be fine if it is still frozen solid or has ice crystals. For any meat, fish, ready meals, or ice cream that fully thawed and became warm, use caution—discard items that were above fridge temperature for more than about 2 hours.
